extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers (PIOs), emergency/public information staff, and emergency management personnel working within NIMS/ICS
extracted.subtask_description: Operational guidance for Public Information Officers performing duties within the Incident Command System (ICS), including procedures to operate a Joint Information System (JIS) and conduct public information across preparedness, response, and recovery phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and coordinated communication
rubrics_metrics.description: During an incident or planned event, coordinated and timely communication is critical to effectively help the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that communications must be coordinated across agencies and delivered in a timely manner to support community needs during incidents and planned events; timeliness and coordination are framed as critical to effective incident management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective and accurate communication can save lives and property, and helps ensure credibility and public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO messaging should be accurate and reliable; accuracy is linked directly to life/property protection and to maintaining credibility and public trust. Avoid misinformation and prioritize correctness of released content.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO role and primary responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Information Officer (PIO) is responsible for communicating with the public, media, and/or coordinating with other agencies, as necessary, with incident related information requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PIO must act as the central point for incident-related information, determining when and how to communicate with different audiences and when to coordinate with partner agencies to meet information requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing and releasing incident information
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO is responsible for developing and releasing information about the incident to the news media, incident personnel, and other agencies and organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIOs must prepare and disseminate information to multiple stakeholder groups (news media, incident personnel, partner agencies/organizations), ensuring releases are appropriate for each audience and coordinated to avoid conflicting messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate within the Incident Command System (ICS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide operational practices for performing PIO duties within the Incident Command System (ICS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO functions should be integrated into the ICS structure; PIOs must follow ICS organizational relationships, use common procedures, and coordinate with other ICS components to ensure unified incident management and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and operate a Joint Information System (JIS) / Joint Information Center (JIC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic procedures to operate an effective Joint Information System (JIS) and guidance addressing actions for JICs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers establishing JIS/JIC arrangements to coordinate public information across agencies, maintain consistent messaging, and manage information flow during incidents; JIS/JIC operation is presented as a core PIO responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address public information across incident phases
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide addresses actions by PIOs for preparedness, incident response, JICs incident recovery, and Federal public information support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO planning and activities should span preparedness (planning and training), response (active incident messaging and coordination), recovery (public information during recovery), and, when applicable, integration of federal public information resources/support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate facilities, equipment, personnel, procedures, and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICS is designed to enable effective and efficient incident management by integrating facilities, equipment, personnel, procedures, and communications operating within a common organizational structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO operations should leverage integrated facilities/equipment and standardized procedures and communications so that messaging aligns with the broader incident management structure; emphasizes using common organizational structures and resources for consistency and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect credibility and public trust as communication objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective and accurate communication helps ensure credibility and public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining credibility and public trust is a stated objective of PIO communications—messages should be transparent, consistent, and evidence-based to preserve public confidence throughout the incident lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate to multiple target audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: PIOs must communicate with the public, media, incident personnel, and other agencies and organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize distinct audience needs and tailor information appropriately (e.g., media briefings vs. operational updates for incident personnel vs. public safety guidance), while coordinating to maintain consistent overall messaging.
